MENTOR: Tile, Caption and Stamp it is. I pulled up a frame at 0 s, but it came back as a tiny flat purple image, so I can't tell you where those three sit on screen from it.

**Here's the idea.** When you parent a layer to another layer, the child picks up the parent's position, scale and rotation. It still keeps its own animation on top of that. A null is an empty layer you use as a handle for this. You put it where the group should turn or scale from, parent the group to it, and animate the null. Hatch already works like this in your comp, since it follows Hatch Rig.

Two things to keep in mind:
- **Children get position, scale and rotation, but not opacity or effects.** If you fade the null, nothing you can see happens.
- **A null never shows up in the render.** It's only a handle and has no look of its own to pass on to the group.

**Your turn:** add a null with Layer > New > Null Object. Before you place it, tell me where Tile, Caption and Stamp should turn or scale from: a corner, the middle of an edge, or the middle of the group. If they'll only slide, you can say so.
